analysis: The code snippet calls `Instant.ofEpochMilli(childSignedWitnessDateMillis).minus(SIGNER_AGE, ChronoUnit.MILLIS)`. The `minus` method may throw DateTimeException if the subtraction cannot be made (e.g., result out of valid Instant range), UnsupportedTemporalTypeException if the unit is not supported (always avoided since ChronoUnit.MILLIS is supported for Instant), and ArithmeticException if numeric overflow occurs during the internal calculation. The context provides no checks on `childSignedWitnessDateMillis` or `SIGNER_AGE` (assumed positive constant). Thus, any extreme value (e.g., near Long.MIN_VALUE or beyond Instant range) can trigger DateTimeException or ArithmeticException. UnsupportedTemporalTypeException is avoided because the unit is always supported.
answer: DateTimeException: Throwing condition not avoided (input may cause result outside Instant range). UnsupportedTemporalTypeException: Throwing condition avoided (ChronoUnit.MILLIS is supported). ArithmeticException: Throwing condition not avoided (input may cause numeric overflow during subtraction).
remark: DateTimeException: Triggered if `childSignedWitnessDateMillis` is extremely low (e.g., near Long.MIN_VALUE) so that subtracting `SIGNER_AGE` milliseconds yields an Instant before the minimum supported instant. ArithmeticException: Triggered if the internal arithmetic (e.g., conversion to seconds and subtraction) causes numeric overflow, which may occur when `childSignedWitnessDateMillis` is close to Long.MIN_VALUE or when the subtraction produces a result outside the long range for seconds/nanos.
